text: The core of fluid mechanics is to reveal the fundamental laws governing fluid motion and to utilize these laws to solve practical problems. It mainly addresses three key questions: How do the physical quantities such as pressure, velocity and density distribute within a fluid when it is at rest or in motion?How are the forces (such as lift, drag and pressure) between a fluid and a solid boundary (such as an aircraft wing, pipeline wall, or dam) calculated?How can the efficiency or safety of engineering equipment be improved by optimizing the fluid motion state (such as designing streamlined structures)? Whether it is the aerodynamics relied upon by aircraft takeoff, the water flow regulation in water conservancy projects, or the analysis of blood flow in the cardiovascular system, all are based on the theory of fluid mechanics.
